rationale: Two critical defects block shipping: the probe path mismatch (inject_bundled_bin_path checks resource_dir root but the shim is at resource_dir/bin/) means PATH injection silently fails on every Windows install, and the absent persist() call means HKCU\Environment is never written — AC5 and spec §3 unmet. Seven additional major findings cover the tautological probe test, stale PowerShell header comment, swallowed eprintln!, untested run_self_update direct-invocation branch, unverified set_var SAFETY contract, and inadequate exit-127 diagnostics; bundle.resources node/cli entries are decision_needed pending EPMCDME-14505 scope clarification. Oversized diff capped coverage of installer.rs and steps.yaml; 2 pre-existing items deferred (install_git_clt non-zero exit fallthrough, download_to_file timeout), 3 dismissed as noise.

findings.title: Bundled shim probe checks wrong subdirectory
findings.problem: inject_bundled_bin_path probes each candidate directory d by checking d.join(n).exists() for each candidate name. tauri.conf.json declares the shim at destination bin/codemie.cmd, so on a production NSIS install the file lives at resource_dir/bin/codemie.cmd. Both the primary branch (current_exe parent = install_dir/) and the resource_dir fallback call probe(d) with the parent directory, not the bin/ subdirectory, so neither branch ever finds the shim.
findings.impact: PATH injection silently returns Err on every production Windows install; the shim directory is never prepended to the process PATH; all cmd.exe codemie invocations in runner.rs and pty.rs fail with command-not-found.
findings.recommendation: Extend both probe branches to also try d.join("bin"): on the resource_dir fallback, return resource_dir.join("bin") when probe(&resource_dir.join("bin")) matches. Apply the same sub-directory check to the current_exe parent branch. Return the matched subdirectory (bin/), not the parent, as bin_dir so that set_var prepends the directory that actually contains codemie.cmd.

findings.title: HKCU\Environment registry write absent
findings.problem: inject_bundled_bin_path calls unsafe std::env::set_var to mutate the process PATH and then immediately returns Ok(()). The Windows persist() function that writes to HKCU\Environment and broadcasts WM_SETTINGCHANGE is implemented in the same file but is never invoked from inject_bundled_bin_path.
findings.impact: The PATH addition exists only for the lifetime of the installer process. Any terminal or application opened after the installer exits cannot find codemie. AC5 ('PATH addition written exclusively to HKCU\Environment') and spec §3 ('inject_bundled_bin_path calls persist()') are both unmet.
findings.recommendation: After the set_var call, call persist(&[dir_str.to_string()]) and surface the error via log::warn! or return it as part of the Err path so callers can distinguish a process-PATH-only update from a full registry write.

findings.title: Probe test asserts file existence, not probe logic
findings.problem: probe_detects_codemie_cmd_shim creates a TempDir, writes codemie.cmd into it, asserts that candidate_bin_names() contains "codemie.cmd" (a static slice, always true), then asserts dir.path().join("codemie.cmd").exists() (trivially true since the test just created the file). The probe closure defined at line 274 and inject_bundled_bin_path are never called.
findings.impact: A regression in the probe logic — wrong iterator predicate, dropped .or_else fallback, or the bin/ subdirectory issue in CR-001 — would not cause this test to fail. The shim directory could silently stop being prepended to PATH at startup with no test signal.
findings.recommendation: Replace the .exists() assertion with a call to the probe closure: extract it as a pub fn probe_dir(d: &std::path::Path) -> bool or test inject_bundled_bin_path with a mock AppHandle pointing to the TempDir, then assert the returned Ok(()) and that the PATH env var was updated.

findings.title: Top-of-file comment still names PowerShell
findings.problem: Line 3 reads "Windows: commands run via `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command`" but shell_cmd on Windows now spawns `cmd.exe /c`.
findings.impact: Any developer reading this file to understand how to write Windows command strings will use PowerShell syntax (e.g., Write-Host, $env:, backtick escaping) and encounter silent failures when those strings are passed to cmd.exe.
findings.recommendation: Update the comment to "Windows: commands run via `cmd.exe /c`".

findings.title: run_self_update direct-invocation branch has no test
findings.problem: The #[cfg(windows)] block in run_self_update that invokes node.exe + cli_entry_path directly when both paths are present (lines 153-168) is never exercised by any test. tests_windows contains only run_capture_runs_via_cmd_and_captures_stdout and run_capture_reports_nonzero_exit_windows, neither of which calls run_self_update.
findings.impact: A bug in argument ordering (cli.as_os_str() before "self-update"), incorrect path serialization, or broken error mapping would silently break Windows self-update whenever the bundled paths are populated, with no test failure.
findings.recommendation: Add a #[cfg(all(test, windows))] test that constructs an AppState with node_exe_path and cli_entry_path pointing to real or mock binaries and asserts run_self_update returns the expected stdout on exit 0 and the correct error message on non-zero exit.

findings.title: Self-update exit 127 gives no root-cause hint
findings.problem: The fallback capture("codemie self-update", None) at line 171 produces a "codemie self-update failed (exit 127): ..." error string that is identical whether the root cause is a failed PATH injection (probe mismatch), a missing sidecar, or an actual CLI error. This path is reachable whenever node_exe_path or cli_entry_path is absent, which is the normal case while CR-001 and CR-002 remain unresolved.
findings.impact: Windows users and support engineers cannot distinguish a broken install from a CLI error based on the error message alone; diagnosing PATH injection failures requires manual investigation.
findings.recommendation: Before the capture() call, check whether node_exe_path or cli_entry_path is empty and log::warn! the specific missing path. Include that context in the Err message returned on non-zero exit.

findings.title: SAFETY comment precondition unverified in Tauri setup()
findings.problem: inject_bundled_bin_path contains `unsafe { std::env::set_var("PATH", &new_path) }` guarded by a SAFETY comment stating it is called before any plugin or thread is started. In Tauri 2.x, setup() runs after the Tokio runtime is initialized; whether internal Tauri threads exist at that point and may concurrently read the environment is not documented. The reachability of a data race is uncertain, but the SAFETY invariant is asserted rather than proven.
findings.impact: Concurrent set_var and env-var reads from an undocumented internal Tauri thread constitute undefined behavior in Rust. The same concern applies to the pre-existing apply_resolved_shell_path set_var call on macOS.
findings.recommendation: Verify in Tauri 2.x documentation or source that setup() is guaranteed to precede any thread that reads the process environment; add a comment citing the specific guarantee. If no such guarantee exists, move PATH setup to a point that clearly precedes Tauri builder initialization.

findings.title: PATH injection failure silently dropped in GUI build
findings.problem: If inject_bundled_bin_path returns Err, lib.rs writes the error to eprintln!. In a packaged Tauri GUI application there is no console; stderr is swallowed by the OS. No in-app log entry, no toast, and no logger::write_line call is made.
findings.impact: A PATH injection failure (currently guaranteed by CR-001 until the probe is fixed) produces no support-visible or in-app trace. The failure is completely invisible until the user attempts to run codemie and receives an unrelated error.
findings.recommendation: Replace eprintln!("{e}") with log::error!("{e}") or commands::logger::write_line(&e, "warn") so the failure appears in the app log visible via the log viewer.

findings.title: node/ and cli/ bundle.resources entries absent
findings.problem: bundle.resources declares only bin/codemie.cmd. The node\node.exe and cli\node_modules\@codemieai\code\dist\index.js target entries are absent. lib.rs setup() populates node_exe_path and cli_entry_path from resource_dir().join("node").join("node.exe") and the cli path respectively, so both fields will be empty PathBufs on every build until the entries are added. Spec §2 states the target layout should be declared in this ticket; EPMCDME-14505 owns source file preparation.
findings.impact: node_exe_path.exists() and cli_entry_path.exists() return false in run_self_update, forcing every Windows self-update through the shim fallback. Declaring the entries without the source files will break tauri build until EPMCDME-14505 delivers the files.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether to declare the resource entries now (coordinating build breakage with EPMCDME-14505) or defer the declaration to EPMCDME-14505. Document the decision and the inter-ticket dependency in the spec or a code comment.
